newsitem.title: USA: Millon Air grounded by FAA after Ecuador crash.
newsitem.headline: Millon Air grounded by FAA after Ecuador crash.

text.p: The U.S. Federal Aviation Administration asked Millon Air to suspend its operations late last week after one of the Miami-based all-cargo airline's Boeing 707s crashed into a residential neighborhood in Ecuador, the FAA confirmed Tuesday.
"The FAA requested that Millon cease operating," said Kathleen Bergen, a spokeswoman for the FAA. "It is a voluntary stand down. They did not surrender their (operating) certificate."
"We have a team inspecting Millon's records," said Bergen. The agency has not yet issued a formal action or consent decree. The FAA had no estimate of how long Millon may be grounded.

On October 22, Millon's 29 year-old aircraft crashed into a densely populated neighborhood in Manta, Ecuador, killing 25 people, hurting 60 more and destroying homes and buildings. Manta is located 480 kms southwest of Quito, the capital of Ecuador.
Repeated calls to Millon executives over the past week were not returned.
Millon grounded its planes on Friday, three days after the crash, said Bergen. Ecuador's aviation administration also suspended Millon's operating permit on Friday.

The plane that crashed in Manta was the same equipment that in February was forced into an emergency landing at Miami International Airport because of problems with the landing gear, according to the FAA documents. Nobody was hurt in the February incident.
Millon has a history of violations, according to FAA documents.

Privately-held Millon had 43 enforcement actions and three incidents since 1985, the documents show. The worst until the Manta crash was on April 28 last year when a Millon DC-8 slid off the runway in Guatemala City and killed six people in a house.

The three-person flight crew was killed in the Manta crash. Capt. Erwin Rodenbeck, 50, co-pilot Hendrick Ripoll, 23, and Ernesto Enciso, 35, all lived in the Miami area. FAA records show no history of accidents, incidents or enforcement problems with any of the three.
Millon handles its own maintenance in Miami.
The aircraft was carrying fish and flowers bound for the United States.
The all-cargo carrier flies exclusively to Latin America.
The company has more than 130 employees. Many of the executives are relatives of Capt. Juan Million, who founded the airline in 1983.
